125521756.title: File:56. Прости, полусложени и сложени скробни зрна од компир (Solanum tuberosum).ogg

ObjectName.value: 56. Прости, полусложени и сложени скробни зрна од компир (Solanum tuberosum)

Categories.value: Solanum tuberosum|Starch|Self-published work|Biology Wikiexperiments|Sara Cvetanoska

ImageDescription.value:
Simple, semi-complex and complex starch of potato (Solanum tuberosum) under microscope

During the process of photosynthesis in plants, sugars are created in the form of starch. Those sugars are stored in the leukoplasts in the cells and form starch grains. We use potatoes to prepare this slide. From the inside of the potato we scraped with a razor blade and a thin smear is made on the object glass. Two drops of water are placed on the object glass, one central larger and one peripheral smaller. A cover glass is placed on it, which is lowered next to the peripheral drop of water and at an angle of 45° it moves towards the middle of the object glass until the moment when the two drops of water merge, during which it is lowered. In this way, the native microscopic slide is prepared and it is ready for microscopy. Simple, semi-complex and complex starch grains are found in potatoes, which are of eccentric type. Simple starch grains have only one center (hilum) from which the concentric layers are formed. Complex starch grains have multiple hilum and in them the concentric layers are formed separately. In the semi-complex starch grains, there are more hilum at first, the concentric layerings are formed separately, and then they tend to be common to the entire starch grain. Starch grains in potatoes are of the eccentric type because the hilum is not located in the center of the starch grain and is moved to one of the ends.

Prepared and performed by Sara Cvetanoska, Institute of Biology, FNSM, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje, Macedonia.
